elements.element: Customer pays no liquidated damages or penalties.
elements.evidence: Rendered Section 7.6 reads: "Customer shall not be liable for any liquidated damages or penalties under this Agreement." This is unconditional, covers both liquidated damages and penalties, and the prior USD 25,000-per-day dependency-delay formula is deleted, leaving no retained formula, instalment or contingent liquidated payment mechanic.

elements.element: Any Customer-payable liquidated amount is only an early-termination fee.
elements.evidence: Condition does not arise: after the edit no Customer-payable liquidated amount of any kind survives (7.6 now negates all liquidated damages and penalties), so there is no non-early-termination liquidated amount to police.

elements.element: The early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: Condition does not arise: the Agreement as redlined contains no early-termination fee or minimum-fee-on-termination mechanic to cap; the only liquidated charge (7.6) has been eliminated outright.

elements.element: The early-termination fee is the sole liquidated amount payable by Customer.
elements.evidence: Condition does not arise: zero liquidated amounts are payable by Customer, which is a stronger outcome than a single capped early-termination fee; no other clause was identified creating a Customer-payable liquidated sum.

reasons: The single operation targets only Section 7.6, the sole Customer-payable liquidated damages provision, and replaces it with one sentence achieving the preferred position; no survival tail, expense language, procedure or unrelated boilerplate was added, so minimality holds.

No words outside the target element were deleted or paraphrased: the deleted USD 25,000 per-day dependency-delay charge is entirely the offending liquidated damages mechanic, and no favourable Customer language was removed.

Intent is preserved: nothing else in Section 7 or elsewhere cross-references 7.6, the mutual liability cap in Section 21.1 is untouched, and Vendor's ordinary remedies (schedule relief, actual damages subject to the cap) survive without contradiction; no undefined terms or dangling cross-references result.
Because the preferred element is fully met by an unconditional negation, the fallback checklist is satisfied vacuously — the drafter need repair nothing in operative language.
